To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the RVE size is not a single number but a function of the applied boundary conditions; (2) RVE size is a random variable with an associated statistical distribution, and (3) for a given boundary condition, the RVE size distribution is independent of the size of the computational domain.

a new concept of gigantic RVE sizes, which are not related to the concept used in homogenization of periodic media, but to the concept of the integral range of a stochastic field.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

, in the case of a stochastic fibrous medium, the RVE size is not a constant number but a statistical variable, whose distribution depends on the contrast of the properties, on the connectivity of the porous phase, and on the integral range of the microstructure.
, in the case of Poisson fibers in a matrix, RVE size is infinite, which means that there is no RVE.
the concept of RVE size can be applied to stochastic microstructures with infinite integral range.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
gigantic RVE sizes are possible for 3D fibrous media.
gigantic RVE sizes are possible, and that a statistical approach is the only way to determine them.
the RVE size of a random microstructure can be estimated through a statistical approach, even in the case of pathological media.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the concept of RVE is not necessarily related to a finite integral range.
the RVE size is not a fixed quantity, but depends on the type of boundary conditions and on the statistical properties of the material.
, for the Poisson fiber network, the RVE size is not related to the size of the microstructure, but to the size of an integral range.
